items.item: All asset sheets follow the selected rules and inventory, preserving identity across views, action states, details and map icons.
P03 shares P01's mailbox geometry with its required cream body; P04 shares P02's cabinet geometry with its required blue-grey body.
All character and object sheets repeat their source records and the rule sheet's palette and light direction in captions, with matching artwork.
All locations preserve Bea and Kit's established identities and the mailbox and cabinet geometry, allowing the specified object body-colour variants.
The four locations share the recorded interaction geometry, ownership channels, state meanings and input-prompt placement while retaining their assigned object pairs and location names.

All scene and interface sheets develop the visual world selected in the note, allowing location-specific surroundings while retaining that direction's silhouettes, object readability and cooperation cues.

requirementChecks.criteria: Read the original file properties: Format: presentation document; at least eight actual pages. Stage: final.

Each board depicts both neighbours cooperating at Mail Court with the supplied mailbox and cabinet identities. The three proposals offer visibly different world or rendering treatments; changes confined to titles or board arrangement do not establish distinct directions. Stylistic exploration is allowed while the objects' identifying geometry and fittings remain recognizable.

The note occupies one page, unambiguously selects one supplied direction, and explains decisions about character outlines, recognition of the interactive objects, and how players recognize cooperation. A name without these explanations, or selection of an unidentified fourth direction, fails.

A single page identifies the selected direction and specifies three world palette colour codes, Bea's #1F4E5F and Kit's #B35C1E ownership colours, usable line and brush instructions, three materials, and a definite lighting direction. World colours, materials and rendering choices are open; omissions or changes to fixed ownership colours fail.

The documented sequence presents three alternatives before selection and carries the chosen direction into subsequent written specifications and the presentation. Page 1 repeats its name. Presentation content identifies all four locations and P01–P04, with reuse assessed separately. Conflicting selections, missing first-page naming or omitted location/object coverage fail; visual development is assessed by the sets and preview checks.

The inventory includes Bea/C01, 1600 mm, Idle/Holding, and Kit/C02, 1750 mm, Idle/Turning, with explicit clothing colours, accessory quantities, silhouettes and their fixed ownership colours/shapes. P01/P03 are 400 × 300 × 600 mm mailboxes with rounded crown, raised vertical front rib, one brass flap knob and rear mounting plate; P02/P04 are 600 × 250 × 800 mm cabinets with flat top, three horizontal vents above a five-spoke wheel and two right-side hinges. Dimensions use width–depth–height order. Body colours are P01 #A84438, P02 #68756B, P03 #D8CCAE and P04 #61798A. Rest/Engaged means closed versus 60-degree-held mailbox flap and stationary wheel/unlit lamp versus clockwise wheel/lit lamp. Missing IDs, unspecified required inventory fields or contradictions fail; unfixed clothing and accessory choices remain open.

Every character, action, object and scene sheet repeats the three source world palette codes and light direction in readable captions and uses the specified palette and lighting in its artwork. Each character or object sheet also repeats its corresponding inventory ID, dimensions and state names. Material shading and the required object body colours may vary within that system. Missing captions, altered record values or visual contradiction of the rules fails.

The presentation contains readable captions repeating the three world palette codes and light direction and includes C01, C02 and P01–P04 with their matching dimensions and state names. Reused specification or asset pages may supply the facts when legible. Missing entries, unreadable reductions or changed values fail.

Bea and Kit retain their inventory clothing colours, accessory quantities and identifying silhouettes across base sheets, action sheets and all gameplay images. Sheet dimensions identify Bea as 1600 mm and Kit as 1750 mm, with depicted relative scale consistent where comparable. Each base sheet includes front, side and back views, Idle plus its character's action state, a close-up and map icon. Bea's additional sheet supplies three views of Holding; Kit's supplies three views of Turning. Viewpoint and pose changes are allowed; swapped identities, lost accessories or missing required views fail.

Each object sheet supplies front, side and back views, Rest and Engaged states, dimensions, a close-up and map icon. P01/P03 share 400 × 300 × 600 mm geometry, rounded crown, raised vertical front rib, one brass flap knob and rear mounting plate; P02/P04 share 600 × 250 × 800 mm geometry, flat top, three horizontal vents above a five-spoke wheel and two right-side hinges. P01 is #A84438 muted red, P02 #68756B grey-green, P03 #D8CCAE cream and P04 #61798A blue-grey. Mailbox state depictions change from closed to a flap held 60 degrees from closed; cabinet states change from stationary wheel/unlit lamp to clockwise operation/lit lamp. Rendering style may vary with the selected direction, but variant geometry changes, wrong fittings or missing sheet components fail.

Read each location identity and verify its pair: Mail Court/S01 uses P01/P02, Wash Passage/S02 P03/P04, Stair Landing/S03 P01/P04 and Roof Garden/S04 P03/P02. Every scene shows Bea, Kit, both operating positions, the connection route and four puzzle-state treatments. Each uses an 8000 × 6000 mm footprint with 1000 mm cells and southwest origin, operating points (2500, 3000) and (5500, 3000) mm, character operating positions (2500, 2500) and (5500, 2500) mm, and 1000 mm reach radii. Locations may differ in surrounding art and perspective; missing locations, substituted object variants or altered interaction geometry fail.

Each sheet names its corresponding location and prints the project title, both object labels, both prompts, 3 s, and the four correct label/counter pairs. It compares controller, touch and keyboard-and-mouse layouts. Bea's prompt is bottom-centred in the left view and means hold the south face button, hold the touch flap control, or hold Space. Kit's prompt is bottom-centred in the right view and means rotate the left stick clockwise, drag the touch wheel clockwise, or hold the left mouse button while dragging the wheel clockwise. Device glyphs may differ; missing input versions, wrong location names, changed actions or swapped player anchors fail.

All three input layouts on every sheet use the stated logical design space with equal left/right player views and a 48-unit inset on all four edges of each view. Text character height is at least 26 logical units. Scaled presentation is acceptable when readable measurements or proportional evidence establish the logical geometry. Text contrast reaches 4.5:1; icons and unavailable controls reach 3:1, and unavailable controls display a lock. A violation in any location or input version fails.

Every location uses colour and shape together for ownership: Bea is #1F4E5F with a circle, Kit is #B35C1E with a triangle. State treatments map Idle 0/2 to a hollow circle and neither input, Ready 1/2 to a half-filled circle and one input, Linked 2/2 to a chain and simultaneous input before the three-second threshold, and Completed 2/2 to a check mark and latched success. Icon styling may follow the chosen direction; swapped mappings, colour-only ownership or inconsistent state meanings fail.

Review the complete 12-second S01 video. Bea holds the P01 flap and Kit turns the P02 wheel clockwise; an attempted overlap breaks before completion, progress returns to zero and the state reflects the remaining input. A fresh uninterrupted three-second Linked 2/2 interval then reaches latched Completed 2/2, illuminates the connection lamp and opens the shared route. Character clothing, accessory counts, proportions, object identities and rendering follow the selected direction and supplied sheets. The Mail Court geometry follows the shared footprint and operating/reach records. Visible interface sequences retain the 1920 × 1080 logical design, equal player views, 48-unit insets, minimum 26-unit text, required 4.5:1 and 3:1 contrast levels, unavailable-control locks, fixed ownership colour/shape pairs and recorded state symbols. Missing reset, shortened successful overlap, incorrect duration or divergence from source assets fails.

requirementChecks.criteria: The presentation has at least twelve pages and visibly reuses identifiable content from every source, including all four character sheets, P01–P04, each location's scene and interface, and frames from the delivered preview. Cropping, resizing and rearrangement are allowed if the source remains recognizable. Mentioning a source without showing its material, omitting any location or object ID, or substituting unrelated artwork fails.

All asset sheets follow the selected rules and inventory, preserving identity across views, action states, details and map icons. P03 shares P01's mailbox geometry with its required cream body; P04 shares P02's cabinet geometry with its required blue-grey body. All character and object sheets repeat their source records and the rule sheet's palette and light direction in captions, with matching artwork.

All locations preserve Bea and Kit's established identities and the mailbox and cabinet geometry, allowing the specified object body-colour variants. The four locations share the recorded interaction geometry, ownership channels, state meanings and input-prompt placement while retaining their assigned object pairs and location names.

All scene and interface sheets develop the visual world selected in the note, allowing location-specific surroundings while retaining that direction's silhouettes, object readability and cooperation cues.
